newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle end mixed, feeders mostly higher.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle end mixed, feeders mostly higher.

text.p: CME live cattle futures remained mixed at the close while feeder cattle finished mostly higher after posting new contract highs.

Live cattle closed 0.100 cent per lb higher to 0.125 lower with June off 0.075 at 64.675 cents. Feeder cattle ended 0.200 cent higher to 0.200 lower with May up 0.175 at 72.200 cents. April and August posted new contract highs of 72.500 and 75.650 cents, respectively.

Disappointment over cash cattle trade at $68 per cwt rather than the $69 expected by some industry watchers, weighed on live cattle futures. But losses were curbed by discount futures hold to cash, traders said.
April trading was considered mostly liquidation ahead of its expiration at 1200 CDT/1700 GMT Wednesday, they said.

Active June showed a mixed trend from early in the day. Although cash cattle trade was not at the higher price expectations, June was already showing an anticipated seasonal drop in cash markets. But traders said there was reluctance to press the market further with June becoming the lead month on Thursday.
R.J. O'Brien bought June and sold April while Cargill Investor Services sold August.
RBH sold June early while R.J. O'Brien, RBH and Lind-Waldock bought, pit sources said.

In live cattle options, commission houses sold June 62 puts and commercials bought August 68 calls early. There was general selling of out of the money June 62 and 63 puts. Volatility was steady to weak, pit sources added.

Feeder cattle ran into profit taking at times but finished strong in nearby months on recent gains in the cash feeder cattle prices and in turn, the CME feeder cattle index. Feeder cattle were expected to stay in tight supply and overall feed costs are expected to be below year-ago prices, traders said.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was up $0.19 at $72.16 per cwt, the highest level since February 22, 1995.

Refco bought May late while Smith Barney and Dean Witter bought August. FIMAT Futures USA and LIT division of First Options bought May early. Cargill Investor Services spread long October, December and February live cattle against short sales and May, August and September futures, pit sources said.
